resources.string: Ask for fingerprint, face or PIN before opening apps

To know when a locked app comes to the front, Able's Accessibility service reads the package name of the app whose window just opened. It does not read the app's content or what you type, and nothing is stored or sent.

It is the same service used by Screen lock and Button shortcuts; each feature works only when you turn it on.

How to turn it off: Android Settings › Accessibility › Able.
Screen lock ready (PIN, pattern or password)

Able shows Android\'s own unlock prompt: fingerprint or face (if enrolled and strong enough for Android), or your device PIN, pattern or password. Able never sees or stores them and has no separate PIN.\n\nThe device must have a screen lock. Without one Android cannot verify you, so App lock stays off rather than locking you out.
Set a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) first.
Ask to unlock when a chosen app opens. Off by default.
Ask to unlock before opening Able, so nobody can turn App lock off.
Stay unlocked after leaving an app

After you unlock an app it stays open while you use it. When you leave it (home screen, recents or another app) it locks again immediately or after the time you choose here. Short dialogs on top of the app, such as permission requests or the share sheet, do not count as leaving.\n\nTurning off the screen always locks every app again.

Only apps with an icon in the launcher are listed. The home-screen app cannot be locked, and Able is controlled by "Lock Able too".

Tip: locking Android Settings also protects the Accessibility settings, so App lock cannot be turned off without unlocking.

Calls are never interrupted: during a call or while the phone rings nothing is locked.

It works at app level, not inside Android: the app opens first and Able covers it right after its window appears, so a glimpse is possible on slow devices. Android does not let Able hide other apps\' content in recents (FLAG_SECURE can only be set by each app itself) or their notifications. It is not active while the phone is locked; after unlocking, a locked app in front asks again. If the Accessibility service is turned off or Android blocks it (for example on managed devices), apps are not locked.
